newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Matches in the German first division this weekend (league position in brackets, kick-offs 1330 GMT unless stated):
Thursday
St Pauli (17) v Hansa Rostock (15) (1800 GMT)

Battle at the bottom of the table between two north German clubs. The Hansa Rostock side which beat Borussia Moenchengladbach last week are unchanged except for key Nigerian striker Jonathan Akpoborie, who is playing for his national team. He will be be replaced by Steffen Baumgart.
Friday
MSV Duisburg (10) v 1860 Munich (6) (1730 GMT)

Duisberg are unbeaten in their last six matches, while 1860 Munich, still battling for a UEFA Cup place, have managed only three draws in their last three away matches and have several key players suspended.
Bayer Leverkusen (2) v Werder Bremen (7) (1800 GMT)

Boosted by an away victory over Stuttgart last week, Bayer Leverkusen will be hoping to keep up the pressure on leaders Bayern. But opponents Werder Bremen will not give in easily as they continue to battle for a UEFA Cup place. Leverkusen have won their last seven home games but have not managed a home victory against Bremen in seven years and may be without Brazilian midfielder Paulo Sergio, who has a thigh injury.
Saturday
Arminia Bielefeld (13) v Borussia Dortmund (3)

Dortmund are expected to field almost the same team which beat Manchester United 1-0 in their European Cup semifinal return leg on Wednesday, including man-of-the-match defender Juergen Kohler. Bielefeld, however, are missing several key players due to injury and suspension, but will be encouraged after inflicting a 5-2 defeat on Cologne last week. Dortmund will again be without Europe's player of the year, libero Matthias Sammer, plagued by injury this season.
Karlsruhe (9) v Hamburg (12)

Middle of the table clash, with Hamburg bolstered by defeat of Schalke last week and only one defeat in their last eight away games. Karlsruhe have won only one of their last seven matches but welcome back defender Gunther Metz after a calf injury. Hamburg likely to be without Argentine Rodolfo Cardoso, who has muscular problems.
Borussia Moenchengladbach (11) v VfB Stuttgart (4)

Stuttgart, a point behind Borussia Dortmund, cannot afford to slip up at Borussia Moenchengladbach, if they are to keep alive their dream of the double after reaching the Cup final two weeks ago. The injury-ridden side, missing seven defenders, will have a fight on their hands but can take reassurance from the fact they have won four of their last five games at Moenchengladbach.
VfL Bochum (5) v Freiburg (18)

VfL Bochum looking to firm their hold on a precious UEFA Cup place after they beat 1860 Munich last week. Bottom team Freiburg are set for relegation, but were boosted last week by a 4-1 thrashing of St Pauli, their first victory in 14 games.
Bayern Munich (1) v Fortuna Duesseldorf (16)

Bayern looking to crush lowly Fortuna Duesseldorf at home and put more distance between themselves and other teams chasing for the title. Bayern are almost at full strength, missing only suspended defender Christian Ziege, likely to be replaced by Marcus Muench. Bayern have won five and drawn one of their last six games, while Fortuna have not won in 10 games.
Schalke (8) v Cologne (14)

Schalke, glowing from winning UEFA Cup final place after their 2-0 victory over Spain's Tenerife, are looking to bounce back from defeat last week at Hamburg and clinch a UEFA Cup place for next season. Cologne, who have not won any of their last eight games, are beset by injuries and players on national duty and can only field an emergency team.
